Incoming freshman can have a tough time adjusting to life as a Division I basketball player.
It can even be unsettling to the stomach — just ask Louisiana Tech guard Dayon Griffin.
"When I came in for my first practice (in 2014) I was throwing up in the garbage can," Griffin recalled Wednesday morning.
Griffin was among five freshmen in Tech's 2014 signing class and is now part of three sophomores — Xavian Stapleton is transferring and Branden Sheppard redshirted — who hope to make a substantial leap in 2016.
Gone are the days where Griffin, guard Jacobi Boykins and center Joniah White can sit back from afar and mentally take notes as seldom used players. There's no more getting their feet wet, because with Tech losing 55 percent of its minutes from 2015, the underclassmen will be needed more than ever.
"It is different because we gotta step up. Last year, I was able to sit and watch people do it," Griffin said. "Now I gotta get out here and do it. I don't have that luxury.
"We're not freshmen coming in. We have more experience. We know we have big goals. We have to step up. My mentality is to come in here and work hard. I know I have to be 10 times better than I was last year. I came in last year not really ready to play right away."
With Alex Hamilton and Erik McCree as the only two main contributors from last year, the first two days of Tech's summer workouts have been centered around the development of players like Griffin and Sheppard with Boykins and White sitting out with undisclosed injuries, although Boykins returned to the court Thursday.
Hamilton and McCree, along with the departures of Stapleton, Speedy Smith, Raheem Appleby and Michale Kyser, accounted for 82 percent of Tech's minutes. In fact, those six players scored 86 percent of the points last year, 50 percent of which came from Stapleton, Smith, Appleby and Kyser.
"You can see there's excitement that they have a chance now to be major impact players on this team," Konkol said.
"We want to have a great summer. Teams are built in the summertime."
Up until Thursday, Boykins hadn't had a chance to show his skills yet, but he's lifted with the team and spent most of Tuesday morning on the floor for moral support.
Boykins plans to morph himself into an all-around player. Last year, Boykins earned a role as the Bulldogs' best 3-pointer shooter (40 percent).
"Obviously you don't want to dismiss his 3-point shooting. You want to make that a strength and make that one where he's just so consistent and making more," Konkol said. "But then we'd like him to be a triple-threat guy where he can pass, dribble, he can attack the basket and still make those catch-and-shoot shots."
Boykins enjoyed a strong finish to 2015, averaging 8.7 points in three NIT games, including an 18-point outburst against Central Michigan.
Griffin, meanwhile, is constantly working on ball handling. The 6-foot-5 guard will compete with Hamilton and freshman Derric Jean for minutes.
Griffin averaged just 1.3 points during a yearlong battle of adjusting to the speed of the college game.
"My experiences, specifically in the conference tournament when I started playing more, I was able to see the actual pace of the game," he said. "I just got to work harder than last year."
To Griffin, the workouts have created a tryout-like environment with four coaches and eight sets of eyes analyzing every move.
Boykins has a different take on it, though, since he viewed every practice with former coach Mike White as a tryout.
However, an expanded role, or even a shot at a starting job, is something they can all agree on.
"That's where the workouts come in or coming in late night on your own to work on your game everyday, maybe even two times a day, trying to get better," Boykins said. "We need to fill Raheem's spot with scoring and Mike Kyser and Speedy, so we just need to come in and work." prompt: Write a 1500-word analytical article, with a professional tone, on the tangible and intangible benefits of implementing a remote work policy, specifically for small businesses. The article should include case studies and real-life examples to support arguments and provide insights into the topic. The article should also delve into the challenges of implementing a remote work policy and provide practical tips for overcoming them. The target audience for the article should be small business owners and managers.
completion:
Introduction:

The remote work trend has been on the rise for the past decade, but it has only gained momentum due to the coronavirus pandemic. The pandemic forced businesses to shift their operations online, and many have implemented remote work policies. The trend has proven to have several benefits for both employers and employees. Besides being a way for companies to stay afloat amidst uncertainties, remote work also provides a better work-life balance for employees. Small businesses can especially benefit from implementing remote policies. In this article, we will look at these benefits and some challenges and tips for implementing them.

Advantages of Remote Work for Small Businesses:

Increased productivity:

A survey conducted in 2019 by Airtasker showed that remote workers spend more time on their work than office employees. The study revealed that remote workers were more productive because they had fewer distractions, took fewer breaks, and had flexibility in their schedules, allowing them to work during their most productive hours. For small business owners, increased productivity means increased revenue and faster growth.

Cost savings:

Rent, utilities, and equipment are some of the costs small business owners have to grapple with. A remote work policy can significantly reduce these costs. By eliminating the need for a physical office, small business owners can save on rent, utilities, and other office-related expenses. Additionally, employees who work remotely incur their transportation and meal expenses, reducing the overhead costs for the business.

Better talent recruitment:

A remote work policy would enable small businesses to recruit top talent from around the globe. With a diverse workforce, small businesses can bring in different perspectives and skillsets, which can lead to innovation and more effective problem-solving. Moreover, part-time remote jobs can appeal to people who want flexibility in their careers or have personal or family commitments.

Retention:

A survey conducted by Owl Labs in 2019 showed that remote workers felt more valued by their employers than office-based employees did. Additionally, the study showed that remote workers were more likely to stay in their jobs than traditional office workers. This is because remote work policies provide a better work-life balance, leading to better overall job satisfaction.

Improved morale and health:

Remote work policies can significantly improve the morale of employees. With the flexibility offered, employees can have more control over their work-life balance, leading to a reduction in stress levels. Additionally, remote work policies can eliminate the need for employees to commute, which can be costly and contribute to employee burnout.

Challenges of Implementing a Remote Work Policy:

While remote work policies have numerous benefits, implementing them for small businesses can be a challenge due to various reasons:

Trust: 

Trust is essential when implementing a remote work policy. The employer has to trust that the employee is working even if they are not physically present in the office. On the other hand, employees must trust that the employer will provide them with the necessary support and training to complete their tasks.

Communication:

In remote work, communication is key. Employers have to find ways to communicate with employees effectively. Moreover, remote employees may feel isolated, leading to less collaborative work than traditional office setups.

Technology:

Remote work policies require employers to provide robust technological support for employees. Unreliable technology can lead to frustration and reduced productivity, which can undo the benefits previously mentioned.

Tips for Overcoming Remote Work Policy Challenges:

Despite the challenges posed by remote work policies, we cannot ignore their potential benefits. Below are some tips for small businesses to overcome these challenges:

Focus on measurable goals:

When implementing a remote work policy, employers should focus on tasks that can be easily measured. Employees should have targets for work output or completed tasks, which can be reviewed regularly.

Regular check-ins:

Regular check-ins can go a long way in maintaining communication levels with employees. These can be scheduled calls, video conferences, or email updates.

Embrace technology:

Employers should embrace technology to ensure effective communication with employees. There is a wide range of apps and software for communication, time tracking, project management, and more.

Provide feedback and recognition:

Providing feedback and recognition to remote employees can help maintain their morale and motivation. It is easy for remote employees to feel isolated, but with proper feedback, they can feel like they are part of their team.

Conclusion:

The use of remote work policies has grown over recent years, but the pandemic has accelerated this trend. Small businesses have several tangible and intangible benefits from implementing remote work policies. Increased productivity, cost saving, better retention, and improved employee morale and health are just some of the benefits. There are also some challenges that small businesses can face when implementing remote work policies. However, with proper planning, execution, and focus on measurable goals and communication, small businesses can harness the potential of remote work policies.

Many a writer with Marion area roots has credited his or her growing up in the area for one attribute or another. The now little remembered author Judson Mortimer Lewis, rather well known in the 1930’s, owned the family farm where he grew up in Highland township until he died, although he never returned. What he was really hanging on to were his deeply personal and cherished memories; perhaps even the place which he considered the source of his talent. For good or bad, there seems to be something extra special about this part of Michigan; good storytellers are born and made here.
Author and publisher and old friends Ron Helmboldt and Ted Parkhurst enjoyed the view from a Marion sidewalk bench last week.
Native Ron Helmboldt comes from a long line of local folks, sportsmen and storytellers. Both his father and his grandfather were barbers, a profession for which storytelling proclivity is a plus.
In his first book, ‘Bicycle Cowboy and other Poems about Growing Up’, Ron gives us a wonderful look into his coming of age in a 1950’s-‘60’s Marion, told in his own poetic, storytelling voice. Bicycle Cowboy is a fine collection remembering personal events, life long friends, family, the joy of Marion, and those gone but not forgotten. Bicycle Cowboy is fresh off the press from Parkhurst Bros. Publishers, based here in Marion and is available locally at their shop on West Main.
If you grew up here during what is often referred to as Marion’s Mayberry days, Ron’s growing up stories about school and being an Eagle in hometown sports (Eagle Football), his neighborhood (Swimmin’ Hole), pals and of course the angst of girls (The Platters, Real Kissin’) will make extra special reading.
Ron also includes a touch of lore (Everett’s Story, Deer Camp Lingo), not often heard here any more. There is also more than a smattering of remembrances from Mel and Fred’s Barber Shop. ‘My Buddy Max’ is a touching and truthful retrospective for an old friend lost. Each reader will hear a grandparent’s voice in “If I had a Nickel….”; a memory from his Marion (via Park Lake) grandparents.
A good growing up memory is a cherished thing. The Marion memories and stories told in Bicycle Cowboy reflect a time not so long ago before video games, cell phones and the iPod; a place we might like to visit again for just a while. This is a highly recommended read for all and will make a great Christmas gift for the reader or Marionite on your list.
Ron Helmboldt is the son of Mel and Lois Holland Helmboldt. He grew up in and around Marion and graduated with the MHS Class of 1963. He went on to graduate from Central Michigan University in 1967 with his teaching degree. He taught history and social studies in Sparta. Ron’s love of sports continued through his teaching career, coaching over 60 seasons of high school sports, mostly wrestling for 38 years. He was elected to the Michigan Wrestling Association Hall of Fame in 2006.
Since retirement in the early 1990›s Ron has concentrated on writing and will be remembered for his popular monthly column in the Marion Millennium. He still hears the call of the outdoors and manages to heed it as often as possible, especially with his old Marion pals.
Ron and his wife Cathy are enjoying life from Manistee these days, and still make frequent trips to the Marion area. Plans are in the works for Ron to speak about his book and visit with readers and old friends at the Marion Public Library soon. In the meantime, Ron continues to write and has plenty of ideas. He has a book of short stories in the works for next year and even has plans to write two Westerns after that. He’s a busy man with a tremendous urge to write. We’ll look for more from this Marionite.

prompt: Write a collection of five short stories, each delving into the themes of betrayal and forgiveness. Ensure that each story explores a different aspect of the themes, and use varying settings and characters to keep the collection engaging. Utilize third-person omniscient narration to provide insight into each character's thoughts and motivations. The stories should be between 1500-2500 words in length and written in a literary style that focuses on developing complex characters and exploring their emotional journeys.
completion:
Story 1: "The Apology"
Julia had been best friends with Katie for as long as she could remember. They had been inseparable since preschool, but now, in their mid-twenties, things were different. Julia had been offered her dream job in a different state and had to leave, and Katie seemed to take it as a personal betrayal. When Julia returned for a visit a year later, hopeful to reunite with her old pal, Katie refused to see her. Julia was heartbroken and felt betrayed by her best friend. After months of trying to mend things, Julia finally wrote Katie a letter apologizing for leaving, even though it was not her intention to hurt her. When Katie read the letter, she realized she had been harsh and unfair. They met up, hugged and cried, and finally forgave each other. 

Story 2: "The Departure"
Hannah had been married to David for ten years. They were happy, or so she thought. Everything came crashing down when he left her for her best friend. Hannah was crushed and felt like her whole world had been turned upside down. She was angry, heartbroken, and didn't know how to move on. Months went by, and David tried to reach out to her to apologize, but Hannah refused to talk to him. One day, out of the blue, she received a letter in David's handwriting, but it wasn't from him. It was from his wife, Sarah. Sarah explained that David had been lost and angry when he left Hannah, but he was begging for forgiveness, and she had forgiven him. Sarah was asking Hannah to do the same. Hannah didn't know how to react to the letter. In the end, she decided that she didn't want to hold on to her anger and bitterness. She forgave David and Sarah, but she never forgot what they did to her.

Story 3: "The Betrayal"
Carla and Steven had been together for three years and were madly in love. Carla thought she had found her soulmate, but then one day she discovered that Steven had been cheating on her with one of her friends. Carla was devastated and felt like she had been betrayed by both of them. She broke up with Steven and cut off all communication with her friend. For months, she couldn't sleep, eat, or think of anything except the betrayal. One day, Carla met Steven by accident, and he apologized. He told her that he had never stopped loving her and that he had been foolish. Carla couldn't believe it, but she saw the pain in his eyes, and it softened her heart a little. She forgave him but refused to be with him again. 

Story 4: "The Estrangement"
Eleanor and her sister, Grace, had always been close, but things changed when Grace went to college. She discovered a new world and new friends, and soon the sisters drifted apart. Eleanor was hurt, and she felt like Grace had betrayed their bond. Eleanor tried to reach out several times, but Grace was always too busy. Then, their mother died suddenly, and the sisters were forced to reconnect while going through her things. They talked about their memories and their feelings, and Eleanor finally revealed how much it had hurt her when Grace left her behind. Grace was shocked and explained that she never meant to hurt her sister. She was just trying to find herself, but she had made a mistake. They hugged, cried and forgave each other.

Story 5: "The Redemption"
Eddie was a thief. He had been stealing since he was a child, and he didn't see any other way of making a living. One day, he stole from a convenience store, but the shop owner caught him in the act. Eddie thought he was going to jail, but the shop owner, Mr. Lee, surprised him. Instead of calling the cops, Mr. Lee told Eddie that he would give him a job and a chance to repay him. Eddie was grateful but didn't trust him at first. As the weeks went by, Eddie worked hard, and Mr. Lee became like a father figure to him. Eddie started to believe that he could be a better person, and he stopped stealing. When he finally saved enough money to repay Mr. Lee, Eddie knew that he had been given a second chance. He apologized and thanked him for everything. Mr. Lee forgave him and offered him a permanent job. Eddie promised he would never let him down again.

prompt: Write a comprehensive proposal that outlines the steps, tools, and techniques you will use to develop an effective sales strategy for a small business. Your proposal should include details on how you will identify target markets, create a compelling value proposition, develop a pricing strategy, and identify key performance metrics to measure success. Additionally, your proposal should detail how you will work with the business owner to implement the sales strategy, measure progress, and make necessary adjustments along the way. Be sure to provide examples and case studies that demonstrate your expertise and experience in developing successful sales strategies for small businesses. Your proposal should be professionally formatted and include visual aids, such as charts and graphs, to help illustrate key points.
completion:
Proposal for Developing an Effective Sales Strategy for a Small Business

Overview:

Our team at [Company Name] has extensive experience in helping small businesses develop and implement effective sales strategies to drive revenue growth. Our approach is based on a thorough analysis of the business, its target markets, its unique selling proposition, and its competitors. We utilize a combination of market research, customer feedback, and industry expertise to create a sales strategy that is tailored to the needs of the business and its customers.

Steps and Tools:

1. Market Research: Our first step is to conduct a thorough analysis of the business's target markets. This involves identifying the key demographic and psychographic characteristics of potential customers, their buying habits, and their preferred channels for communication and purchasing. We will use a combination of primary and secondary research techniques, including surveys, focus groups, interviews, and data analysis tools such as Google Analytics, to gather information about the market.

2. Competitive Analysis: Once we have a clear understanding of the target markets, we will conduct a competitive analysis to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the business's competitors. This includes analyzing their marketing and sales strategies, pricing, product offerings, and customer feedback.

3. Unique Selling Proposition: Based on the market research and competitive analysis, we will help the business identify its unique selling proposition (USP) – the qualities that make it stand out from its competitors. This will form the foundation of the sales strategy.

4. Value Proposition: We will help the business create a compelling value proposition that communicates its USP to potential customers. This includes identifying the benefits of the product or service, the problems it solves, and the emotional appeals that will resonate with the target audience.

5. Pricing Strategy: We will develop a pricing strategy that is competitive, profitable, and reflects the value of the product or service. This includes analyzing the costs of production, the pricing strategies of competitors, and the perceived value of the product or service to customers.

6. Sales Channels: We will help the business identify the most effective sales channels for reaching its target markets, based on the preferences of the customers and the strengths of the business. This may include e-commerce, social media, email, phone, or in-person sales.

7. Key Performance Metrics: We will identify the key performance metrics that will be used to measure the success of the sales strategy. This may include revenue, conversion rates, average order value, and customer lifetime value.

Implementation and Evaluation:

1. Sales Plan Development: We will work with the business owner to develop a comprehensive sales plan that outlines the tactics, timelines, and metrics for achieving the sales goals. This includes the creation of a sales funnel, sales scripts, marketing materials, and sales training for the sales team.

2. Coaching and Support: We will provide ongoing coaching and support to the business owner and the sales team throughout the implementation of the sales strategy. This includes regular check-ins, feedback sessions, and adjustments to the strategy based on data and feedback.

3. Data Analysis and Reporting: We will regularly analyze the sales data and provide reports to the business owner to track progress, identify trends, and make informed decisions. We will also provide recommendations for adjustments to the sales strategy based on the data analysis.

Examples and Case Studies:

Our team has worked with numerous small businesses to develop and implement successful sales strategies. In one example, we worked with a local restaurant to develop a value proposition focused on the quality of the ingredients and the unique atmosphere of the restaurant. We created a pricing strategy based on the perceived value of the food and the experience, and helped the restaurant owner implement an email marketing campaign to reach potential customers.

Another example is a small online retailer that was struggling to compete with larger retailers. We helped the retailer identify its USP – personalized customer service – and created a value proposition that emphasized the benefits of this service. We helped the retailer implement a chatbot on the website to provide immediate customer support, and created a referral program to incentivize existing customers to refer new customers.

Conclusion:

Our team at [Company Name] has a proven track record of helping small businesses develop and implement effective sales strategies that drive revenue growth. Our approach is based on a thorough analysis of the business, its target markets, and its competitors, and is tailored to the unique needs of the business and its customers. With our coaching and support, the business owner and sales team will have the tools and techniques they need to achieve their sales goals and grow the business.

prompt: Write a fictional short story of no more than 2000 words, in third person point of view, about a young man who is torn between his love for a woman and his duty to his family's business. The story should include at least two primary external conflicts, one of which should be related to the protagonist's love interest, and the other which should relate to his family's business. The resolution of the story should be realistic and emotionally satisfying for the reader. Use vivid sensory details and descriptive language to create a strong sense of setting and character.
completion:
Ben had always idolized his family. They had started a small manufacturing business in their hometown and through years of hard work and dedication, they had built it up into an empire. Ben had grown up watching his parents work tirelessly, pouring their blood and sweat into the company. They had impressed upon Ben and his siblings the importance of family, loyalty and hard work, and these values had become the cornerstone of Ben's life.

As Ben grew up, he began to fall in love with a beautiful young woman named Katie. She was bright, funny and full of life - everything that Ben wanted in a partner. But as much as he loved her, he also felt the burden of his family's expectations weighing heavily on his shoulders. His parents had always anticipated that their children would take over the business when they retired, and Ben knew that this was not just a desire, but a responsibility.

His heart and his head were at odds with one another, and Ben felt trapped. He couldn't bear to disappoint his parents, yet he couldn't bear to let Katie go. He worried that if he chose her, he would be turning his back on his family, on everything that they had worked for.

As he and Katie grew closer, Ben noticed that she was becoming increasingly frustrated with him. She could sense that something was holding him back, and she pushed him to open up to her. One night, as they lay in bed together, Ben found himself pouring out all of his worries and fears to her. He told her that he loved her more than anything in the world, but he didn't know how to reconcile that with his obligations to his family.

Katie listened carefully, and then she told him something that made him stop and think. "Ben," she said, "I love you too. And I want to spend the rest of my life with you. But if you can't be happy in your own life, if you can't be true to yourself, then how can you ever make me happy?"

prompt: Write a detailed essay on the topic "Discuss the potential impact of gravitational waves on the study of dark energy in our own galaxy", focusing on recent developments in the field and the implications for our understanding of the universe as a whole. Your essay must include a detailed analysis of the current state of research on gravitational waves, as well as a critical examination of the limitations and challenges facing researchers in this area. In addition, you should provide examples of specific experiments, observations, or technologies that are helping to advance our understanding of dark energy, and explain how these findings are contributing to the broader field of astrophysics. Finally, your essay should conclude with a reflection on the implications of these investigations for our fundamental understanding of the physical laws that govern our universe.
completion:
Gravitational waves are ripples in the fabric of space-time caused by the acceleration of massive objects. These waves were predicted by Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity in 1916, but it was not until 2015 that they were directly detected by the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory (LIGO) collaboration. Since then, gravitational wave astronomy has emerged as a rapidly growing field with the potential to revolutionize our understanding of the Universe. One area of particular interest is the study of dark energy, and in this essay, we will discuss the potential impact of gravitational waves on our understanding of this enigmatic force.

Dark energy is a mysterious substance that is believed to make up approximately 70% of the total energy density of the universe. It is responsible for the exponential expansion of the universe that has been observed since the Big Bang. Dark energy is a difficult subject to study because it does not interact with light, making it invisible to telescopes. However, recent advancements in technology have led to the development of new tools and techniques that are helping scientists to study dark energy in unprecedented detail.

One promising avenue for studying dark energy is through the observation of gravitational waves emitted by merging black holes or neutron stars. When two massive objects merge, they emit gravitational waves that carry information about the masses and spins of the objects, as well as the properties of space-time around them. By studying the properties of the gravitational waves that are emitted, scientists can learn about the masses and spins of the objects, as well as how they are distributed throughout the galaxy.

One of the key advantages of studying gravitational waves for dark energy research is that they are not affected by the same astrophysical effects that can complicate other methods of observation, such as galaxy surveys or supernova observations. This means that gravitational wave observations can provide an independent check on other measurements of dark energy, potentially helping to reduce uncertainties and improve our understanding of this elusive force.

Recent observations have already yielded some interesting results. For example, studies of gravitational waves emitted by merging black holes have revealed that the objects involved are clustered in certain regions of the universe, which could have implications for our understanding of dark energy. Additionally, the observation of binary neutron star mergers has provided new insights into the properties of neutron stars, which could have implications for the equation of state of dark energy.

Despite the exciting potential of gravitational waves for dark energy research, there are also significant challenges associated with this approach. One of the biggest challenges is the fact that gravitational waves are extremely weak, making them difficult to detect from distant sources. This means that detectors like LIGO are only sensitive to events within our own galaxy, limiting the scope of observations. As a result, it is likely that we will need to wait for the development of more sensitive detectors or the detection of closer events to make significant progress in this area.

Another challenge is the fact that gravitational wave observations are subject to a number of sources of noise, including environmental effects and technical limitations of the detectors themselves. These sources of noise can make it difficult to distinguish between signals from real astrophysical events and spurious noise, which can lead to false positives or missed opportunities to make significant discoveries.

Despite these challenges, researchers are continuing to make progress in the field of gravitational wave astronomy, with new experiments, technologies, and facilities being developed all the time. For example, new detectors like the Einstein Telescope and the Cosmic Explorer are planned that will be even more sensitive than current detectors, potentially allowing for the detection of events from much farther away. Additionally, new observational techniques like the use of pulsar timing arrays or cosmic microwave background measurements may also offer new avenues for studying dark energy through gravitational wave observations.

In conclusion, the study of gravitational waves has the potential to significantly impact our understanding of dark energy in our own galaxy, providing independent checks on other methods of observation and potentially offering new insights into the properties of this elusive force. However, there are also significant challenges associated with this approach, including the weakness of the signals, environmental effects, and technical limitations of the detectors. Despite these challenges, researchers are continuing to make progress in the field, with new experiments and technologies being developed all the time. Ultimately, the study of gravitational waves is a key area of research for advancing our understanding of the physical laws that govern the universe, and it is likely to be an active area of investigation for years to come.

prompt: Please conduct a detailed case study on a community of your choice that has effectively implemented sustainable practices. Your study should include an analysis of the community's sustainability goals, the actions they have taken to achieve those goals, and their achievements and challenges in implementing sustainable practices. Additionally, your case study should also evaluate the economic, environmental, and social impacts of the community's sustainability efforts. Please provide concrete examples, data, and relevant sources to support your analysis, and conclude the study with recommendations for how other communities can adopt similar sustainable practices.
completion:
Case Study: The City of Vancouver

Introduction

The City of Vancouver, located in British Columbia, Canada, is a community that has effectively implemented sustainable practices. The city is recognized as a leader in sustainability, with a long history of putting sustainability at the forefront of its policies and initiatives. This case study will analyze the sustainability goals of Vancouver, the actions the city has taken to achieve those goals, and their achievements and challenges in implementing sustainable practices. Moreover, this study will also evaluate the economic, environmental, and social impacts of the city's sustainability efforts. Finally, this study will provide recommendations for how other communities can adopt similar sustainable practices.

Sustainability Goals and Actions

The City of Vancouver has set ambitious sustainability goals to achieve a sustainable future. One of the goals is to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 80% below 2007 levels by 2050. To achieve this goal, Vancouver has implemented various measures. For instance, Vancouver has adopted policies that encourage the use of public transport, bicycles, and walking. In addition, Vancouver has implemented a carbon tax, where businesses are required to pay a fee for their greenhouse gas emissions. The revenue generated from the carbon tax is used to fund sustainable initiatives such as public transit. Moreover, Vancouver has invested in renewable energy, such as hydro, wind, and solar power, to reduce its reliance on fossil fuels.

Another goal of the city is to create a zero-waste community by 2040. To achieve this goal, Vancouver has implemented several measures, such as the Green Bin Program. This program provides residents with an organic waste collection system, where food scraps, yard waste, and other organic materials are composted into nutrient-rich soil. The city has also implemented a curbside recycling program that collects various types of recyclable materials, such as paper, glass, and plastic.

Achievements and Challenges

The City of Vancouver's efforts towards sustainability have been successful. For instance, the city has reduced GHG emissions by 6% below 2007 levels as of 2018. Moreover, Vancouver has the lowest carbon footprint per capita of any city in North America. The city has also achieved a 50% waste diversion rate, meaning that half of all waste generated in Vancouver is recycled or composted.

However, Vancouver faces some challenges in implementing sustainable practices. One of the most significant difficulties is the high cost of sustainable initiatives. For instance, investing in renewable energy and building infrastructure for public transit is expensive. Moreover, there is a lot of resistance from some businesses and residents towards sustainable initiatives. Many see them as unnecessary or too expensive.

Impacts of Sustainability Efforts

The City of Vancouver's sustainability efforts have had significant impacts on the economy, environment, and social well-being of the community.

Environmental Impacts:

The city's initiatives towards reducing GHG emissions have helped to mitigate climate change, reducing the likelihood of extreme weather events such as floods, droughts, and heatwaves.

The curbside recycling program and Green Bin Program have reduced the amount of waste sent to landfills, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

Economic Impacts:

The implementation of sustainable practices has created jobs in various fields such as public transit, renewable energy, and waste management.

The reduction in GHG emissions has saved the city money by reducing the need for emergency management in case of extreme weather events.

Social Impacts:

The investments in public transit have made transportation more accessible and affordable, promoting social equity.

The Green Bin Program has provided residents with free nutrient-rich compost for their gardens, promoting urban agriculture.

Recommendations

To implement similar sustainable practices, communities can take the following recommendations:

Set ambitious and achievable sustainability goals that cover various aspects of sustainability.

Encourage businesses and residents to adopt sustainable practices by offering incentives such as tax credits or rebates.

Invest in renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure, such as public transit, biking, and walking infrastructure.

Educate the community about the benefits of sustainability and engage them in the process of achieving sustainable goals.

Conclusion

The City of Vancouver has effectively implemented sustainable practices, achieving significant success in reducing GHG emissions, increasing waste diversion rates, and creating a more sustainable community. The city's efforts have had positive impacts on the environment, economy, and social well-being of the community. To adopt similar sustainable practices, communities can set ambitious sustainability goals, invest in sustainable infrastructure, offer incentives, and educate their communities about the benefits of sustainability. By doing so, communities can create a more sustainable future, mitigating the worst impacts of climate change, and promoting social equity.

Staffing shortages at the Federal Emergency Management Agency during the 2017 hurricane season and other logistical shortcomings hampered the response after Hurricane Maria walloped Puerto Rico, the agency says in a new report.
The after-action report, released Thursday, reveals the agency also dealt with contracting personnel strains across disasters in 2017, had trouble tracking billions of dollars in meal and water supplies, and remains behind targets for disaster workforce certifications.
Hurricane Maria’s devastation of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands proved particularly trying, with FEMA failing to utilize previous training exercises that suggested that Puerto Rico would need intensive federal help.
One official who works with state government leaders said, in the case of Puerto Rico, lack of electricity and communications were the biggest disaster response struggles.
FEMA notes that key supplies in Puerto Rico, such as cots and tarps, were moved weeks before the storm to St. Thomas to help with recovery there from Hurricane Irma. That meant when Maria struck Puerto Rico, there was an "immediate deficit of commodities" there, requiring supplies to be airlifted in.
The Caribbean Distribution Center warehouse in Puerto Rico had no cots or tarps left and only 180 units of blue roof sheeting, 1 percent of total inventory, when Maria hit, the report says. That’s a scenario where contingencies become important, McLeod said.
Much of the problem was that FEMA underestimated needs ahead of the 2017 hurricane season and was forced to rely on crisis action planning to cover shortfalls.
Power outages were estimated to affect 73 percent of the island should a hurricane, earthquake or tsunami strike, when in reality 100 percent of the territory was affected—a 27 percent planning gap.
The report concludes that 2017’s three hurricanes, coupled with wildfires in California, required “major adaptations” to FEMA operations that remain a work in progress one month into the 2018 season.
More disaster survivors registered for FEMA assistance in the aftermath of Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria and the California wildfires than in the previous 10 years combined.
In Puerto Rico, Maria rendered 95 percent of cell towers inoperable, which has FEMA currently refining land mobile radio to satellite communications.
“As a result local, territorial, and federal agencies faced difficulties knowing what was needed and where in the immediate aftermath of the storm,” Long wrote.
Internet access may even be more critical than cellular communications moving forward because of people’s reliance on mobile applications, McLeod said.
FEMA found itself coordinating entire community logistics in Puerto Rico and facilitating meal and water transport from staging areas to survivors, which “should largely be managed and coordinated at the state or territory level,” according to the report.
McLeod agreed FEMA is there to support states and territories, which are in turn responsible for distributing resources on the ground.
The agency’s 2018-2022 Strategic Plan that Long implemented emphasizes the need to increase state capacity and improve intergovernmental coordination to take some of the burden off of the federal government.
FEMA already consolidated facilities to increase capacity last hurricane season, and is now calling for revisions to the National Response Framework and Response Federal Interagency Operational Plan that will hopefully quicken stabilization of lifelines like power, communications, commodities and transportation in future disasters.
The agency also proposes establishing a public-private Interagency Power Task Force that can turn into a crisis action planning cell during disasters.
And this hurricane season has seen commodities kept at locations in the Caribbean increased more than sixfold—enough to support 600,000 survivors for three days—and about 300 new emergency generators added to FEMA’s inventory in advance of crises. There are now five commodity storage warehouses on Puerto Rico, instead of one.
Housing was a final FEMA shortfall during the 2017 hurricane season that the agency is working to address by lessening the inspection burden for survivors.
“FEMA challenges its federal partners to think beyond current policy, regulatory, and legislative restrictions to determine how best to deliver post-disaster housing to the nation’s affected citizens after any given disaster,” reads the report.

What other applications could the findings of this study have beyond microfluidics?: Scientific discoveries often arise from noticing the unexpected. Such was the case when Stanford researchers, studying a tiny device that has become increasingly important in disease diagnostics and drug discovery, observed the surprising way it funneled thousands of water droplets into an orderly single file, squeezing them drop by drop, out the tip of the device.
Instead of occurring randomly, the droplets followed a predictable pattern. These observations led graduate student Ya Gai and Sindy K. Y. Tang, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering, to deduce mathematical rules and understand why such rules exist. The work was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. It all started with an effort to design tiny devices called microfluidic chips, designed to automate and expedite biomedical research.
In the past, lab experiments involved using a dropper to deposit biological specimens into a test tube for observation. But microfluidic devices work much more efficiently. About the size of a postage stamp, they are made of silicone containing many thin channels through which researchers can pump tiny amounts of fluids. The devices allow researchers to place a specimen into a droplet of water surrounded by a thin film of oil. That droplet becomes the test tube. The oily film keeps each droplet and specimen separate.
The microfluidic chips developed in the Tang Lab can create millions of these specimen-bearing droplets quickly. The steadily streaming droplets are ultimately funneled in single file past an instrument that peers at the specimen inside the droplet.
“While studying the flow physics of the droplets in the funnel, we observed that, contrary to our expectations, the droplets juggle past each other in a very orderly manner as they squeeze from the wide end to the narrow end of the funnel, which can fit only one drop at a time,” Tang said.
The team saw packs of drops sliding against each other, something that is more typically seen in solid crystals. ”That caused us to consider concepts from solid mechanics,” Tang said. She invited Wei Cai, another mechanical engineer who studies how atoms move in crystals, to join the effort.
“Stanford Mechanical Engineering is a great place to be as the environment promotes collaborative efforts, in this case between microfluidics and solid mechanics,” Tang said.
While water droplets are squishy and metals seem solid, if you zoom past what is visible, tiny droplets coated in oil bear some resemblance to metal atoms wrapped in electron clouds.
“They both occupy space,” Cai said. “You can’t put two atoms or two droplets in the same spot.” The researchers found that when force is applied — such as when microfluidic pressure is used to force droplets through the funnel — they squeeze against each other and move according to the laws of mechanics.
When crystals are deformed, defects called dislocations form and move through the lattice to shuttle the atoms around. It turns out that the periodic pattern of droplets is the result of dislocation dynamics that also occur when crystalline solids are deformed.
“Beyond the immediate relevance to microfluidics, we believe our findings could one day be applied to forming nanocrystals into precise shapes,” Tang said. Researchers do not yet have a way to exert the sort of steady pressure on metal atoms that microfluidic chips can do with oil-separated water droplets.
The corresponding process for metal forming is called extrusion — it’s also what happens when we press the wide end of the toothpaste tube to deposit a dab on our brush. If technologists find a way that could extrude atoms through a nanoscale channel, one could imagine the atoms funneling along as do the water droplets in the microfluidic channel.
And if or when such nanoscale extrusion becomes possible with metallic atoms, this experiment suggests that it may be used to produce nanowires with diameter precision down to a single atom.
“We saw something puzzling, we asked the right questions and we learned something useful not just to the problem we are studying, but also to an entirely different field, in this case how one might go about manufacturing nanocrystals,” Tang said.
An additional author on the paper is Chia Leong, a visiting scholar in the Tang Lab. Sindy Tang is a member of Stanford Bio-X and Stanford ChEM-H. This work was supported by the National Science Foundation.
completion: The findings of this study could have applications beyond microfluidics in the field of nanotechnology. If a way is found to exert steady pressure on metallic atoms, similar to the pressure exerted on water droplets in microfluidic chips, it could be used to produce nanowires with diameter precision down to a single atom. The study suggests that the same dislocation dynamics observed in the flow of water droplets in microfluidic devices could also occur in metals during extrusion, which could lead to the manufacturing of nanocrystals. Furthermore, the study highlights the value of interdisciplinary collaboration in scientific research, as the combination of microfluidics and solid mechanics led to unexpected discoveries and potential applications.

prompt: Create a comprehensive marketing strategy for a new line of luxury watches that emphasizes the unique features and benefits of the watches, highlights the target audience, selects appropriate marketing channels and tactics, includes a budget and timeline, and measures the effectiveness of the campaign through clear metrics and KPIs. Ensure that the strategy is on-brand, engaging, and relevant to the luxury watch market.
completion:
Introduction:

This marketing strategy will focus on launching a new line of luxury watches that offers unique features and benefits to the target audience. We will target a high-income audience who values luxury, impeccable craftsmanship, and design excellence. Our aim is to convince the audience that our new line of luxury watches is synonymous with class, sophistication, and opulence. Our marketing strategy will focus on highlighting the unique features and benefits of the watches, selecting appropriate marketing channels and tactics, setting a budget and timeline, and measuring the effectiveness of the campaign through clear metrics and KPIs.

Target Audience:

Our target audience consists of high-income individuals who value luxury and opulence. These individuals are generally aged 30 and above, and have a high disposable income. They are sophisticated, fashionable, and are always looking to make a statement with their fashion choices. Our target audience is not just looking for a watch that tells time, but for a timepiece that is a symbol of their success and their lifestyle. They want something unique, timeless, and magnificent that will last for many years to come. They are also tech-savvy and are always on the lookout for new and innovative products.

Unique Features and Benefits:

Our new line of luxury watches offers unique features and benefits that set them apart from other luxury watches. These features and benefits include:

•	Swiss-made movement for precision and accuracy.
•	High-quality materials such as stainless steel, diamonds, and leather for durability and opulence.
•	Unparalleled design excellence that combines modern aesthetics with traditional watchmaking techniques.
•	Advanced technology such as Bluetooth connectivity and health tracking features.
•	A variety of styles to suit different preferences and occasions.

Marketing Channels and Tactics:

To ensure that our new line of luxury watches reaches our target audience, we will employ the following marketing channels and tactics:

•	Social Media Marketing – we will use social media platforms such as Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook to showcase our watches and reach our audience.
•	Influencer Marketing – we will collaborate with fashion influencers and celebrities to promote our brand and watches.
•	Public Relations – we will engage with targeted publications, media outlets, and journalists to increase public interest in our watches.
•	Event Marketing – we will host exclusive launch events and VIP parties to showcase our watches and attract high-end clients.
•	Search Engine Optimization (SEO) – we will optimize our website for search engines to increase online visibility.

Budget and Timeline:

Our budget for this marketing campaign will be $500,000, which will be allocated as follows:

•	Social Media Marketing – $100,000
•	Influencer Marketing – $75,000
•	Public Relations – $100,000
•	Event Marketing – $150,000
•	SEO – $75,000

We will launch our marketing campaign in the summer of 2022, with the following timeline:

•	Social Media Marketing – June 2022 – September 2022
•	Influencer Marketing – June 2022 – August 2022
•	Public Relations – July 2022 – September 2022
•	Event Marketing – August 2022 – September 2022
•	SEO – June 2022 – September 2022

Metrics and KPIs:

To measure the effectiveness of our marketing campaign, we will use the following metrics and KPIs:

•	Website Traffic – we will track website traffic to determine the effectiveness of our SEO campaign.
•	Social Media Engagement – we will track engagement levels on social media to determine the effectiveness of our social media campaign.
•	Influencer Engagement – we will track the engagement levels of our influencers to determine the effectiveness of our influencer campaign.
•	Publicity – we will track media mentions and articles about our watches to determine the effectiveness of our PR campaign.
•	Sales – we will track sales revenue to determine the overall effectiveness of our marketing campaign.

Conclusion:

Our marketing strategy for a new line of luxury watches leverages unique features and benefits to reach out to our high-income target audience. We will deploy a mix of social media marketing, influencer marketing, public relations, event marketing, and SEO. Our campaign will be measured through clear metrics and KPIs, which will help us measure the return on investment and refine our marketing tactics as required. With the right mix of marketing channels, we believe that our new line of luxury watches will be a resounding success in the luxury watch market.

CDC today released Health, United States, 2016, the 40th annual report on the health of the nation from the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to the President and Congress.
This year’s report features a Chartbook on Long-Term Trends in health and health care delivery over the past 40 years. From declines in cigarette smoking and increases in prescription drug use to changes in expenditures for hospitals and home health care, the annual report also explores population changes that have affected patterns of disease, as well as health care access and utilization since 1975. The 27 charts and 114 tables present birth rates and infant mortality, life expectancy and leading causes of death, health risk behaviors, health care utilization and insurance coverage, and health expenditures.
Between 1975 and 2015, life expectancy increased for the total population and for males and females. However, between 2014 and 2015, life expectancy declined by 0.1 years for the total population, 0.2 for males, and 0.1 for females.
The infant mortality rate decreased 63 percent, from 16.07 to 5.90 deaths per 1,000 live births between 1975 and 2015.
Between 1975 and 2015, the age-adjusted heart disease death rate decreased 61 percent from 431.2 to 168.5 deaths per 100,000 population. The age-adjusted cancer death rate decreased 21 percent from 200.1 to 158.5 deaths per 100,000 population. Heart disease and cancer remain the top two causes of death in the United States.
Between 1974 and 2015, the age-adjusted prevalence of current cigarette smoking declined from 36.9 percent to 15.6 percent among persons aged 25 and over.
The age-adjusted percentage of adults aged 20 and over with obesity increased steadily from 22.9 percent in 1988–1994 to 37.8 percent in 2013–2014.
Prescription drug use increased for all age groups between 1988-94 and 2013-14. Among adults 65 and over, use of five or more prescription drugs in the past 30 days increased from 13.8 percent to 42.2 percent during the same period.
The percentage of persons with an overnight hospital stay was lower in 2015 than in 1975 for males and females under age 75, and was not significantly different in 2015 than in 1975 for males and females aged 75 and over.
Between 1975 and 2014, the number of community hospital beds per 1,000 resident population fell by almost one-half from 4.6 to 2.5. The average length-of-stay per hospital stay fell by almost one-third from 7.7 to 5.5 days, and occupancy rates declined almost 16 percent from 75.0 percent to 62.8 percent.
Other types of care increased from 10.6 percent to 13.2 percent.
Between 1978 and September 2016 (preliminary data), the percentage of children under age 18 who were uninsured decreased from 12.0 percent to 5.0 percent; the percentage with Medicaid coverage increased from 11.3 percent to 39.2 percent; and the percentage with private coverage decreased from 75.1 percent to 53.5 percent.
The rural (nonmetropolitan) share of the population declined between 1970 and 2015; the suburban share of the population increased.
The full report is available at https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/hus/.
How has the prevalence of cigarette smoking and prescription drug use changed over the past 40 years according to the report?
